horizon_p95_lt_1.why: A canopy edge does not fit the 180 vertex cap at tau 1.0, so the published line is the tau 1.5 rung (150 vertices) and sits up to 1.5 degrees above the profile, on top of the profile's own foliage error (p95 1.32 against the truth, 1.07 against the bin maximum). The limit is the gate's 1.0 plus that 1.5; a coarser line is not covered (#1059).

no_unresolved_boundary.why: 30 of 720 bins are unresolved (17 Low, 10 Unknown, 3 Tall), each published closed at 90 degrees, and 5 of the Low bins are truth bins with a range over 2 degrees. 36 bins is 5 percent of the profile, the safe-direction share the scorer already tolerates for Measured bins that are not visible; measured_share still asks for 85 percent of the expected bins (#1059).

measured_is_honest.why: p99 reads 3.43 against 2.0 because Measured bin 591 publishes 12.7 degrees where the truth maximum is 21.4 and bin 707 13.4 where it is 17.4 (an edge that falls inside the bin), and bin 436 is 14.0 degrees too high; the rest of the p99 is the 2 to 5 degree error of canopy edges. Bins 273 to 275 (10.7 to 11.1 where the truth is 27.1 to 29.5, a crown 11 degrees tall over open sky) are no longer Measured since #1058: a bin is Measured only where a step was observed, so a dark structure the walk could not account for above the boundary makes the bin Unknown. Capping the line cannot excuse the remaining bins, so no limit is ruled; the ruling goes stale, and fails the case, when the gate passes (#1059).
